galley what it's for the round the cli licensing setup

A document two parties revise in rounds

galley

Edit the draft. Instruct the agent. Read what the round changed.

galley opens a Markdown file in the browser. You make direct edits — they apply immediately — and leave instructions on the passages you want the agent to handle. Revise sends the round. The agent revises the .md file itself; its changes land, they are not proposals. You read the diff, instruct again if you need to, and Approve when it's right. Markdown in, Markdown out, no markup on disk.

what it's for

The draft is the conversation.

An agent writes a plan, a spec, a PR description. You read it and you have notes. Pasting them into a chat loses the place they belong; hand-editing the file loses the agent. In galley the document is where both of you work: you fix what's faster to fix yourself, point at what isn't, and the agent answers by changing the file. A comment is an instruction discharged by the revision — not a thread, not a proposal you then have to accept.

direct edits, applied

Retype a sentence, cut a paragraph, fix the heading. Your edits are in the file the moment you make them — no accept, no reject, no suggestion mode.

instructions on passages

Select a span and say what's wrong with it, or instruct the whole document. Revise sends every instruction at once, each one anchored to the text it's about.

the agent revises the file

The agent edits the .md with its own tools. While it holds the round galley watches the file and streams every save into your browser; one acknowledgement commits the round.

every round is a version

Your send is a version; the agent's return is the next. History shows each one beside the instruction that produced it, with a sentence-level diff computed between clean documents — never stored in them.

the round

One mechanism: commit on send.

The reviewer holds the document in the browser; the agent holds it as a file. A round is one exchange between them, and both sides of it are clean Markdown. Nothing galley adds while you work — highlights, instruction notes — survives the press of Revise.

revise Pressing Revise commits your version and sends the round: the captured instructions, each with the quoted passage it anchors to. A sent round is no longer pending — what the agent receives is what you sent, not whatever you typed next.
the agent's turn The agent edits the file directly and saves as often as it likes; each save appears in your browser. galley ack --state answered commits its round, once, for the whole revision. Its changes are applied, not proposed. There is nothing to accept.
what changed The diff is galley's own, computed between the two versions — sentence-level, so a rewrite reads as one change rather than six fragments, and a typo doesn't light up the paragraph. The agent can annotate a change with which instruction it answers; the list itself is galley's, derived from the documents.
cannot If an instruction genuinely can't be done, galley cannot --why records a round with the document unchanged. A report, not an argument. You answer it with a different instruction.
approve Approve ends the review with the document as it stands. Versions live in .galley/versions/, gitignored by default; instructions are recorded in the ledger with the round that carried them. The file on disk is only ever the document.
any agent Works with anything that can edit a file. galley channel is an MCP server that pushes each Revise into a running session as a channel event (Claude Code, launched with its channel flag); galley wait is the same loop for a shell. Cold start instead? --on-revise spawns a session with galley agent-prompt as its instructions.

The reading commands — comments, pending, wait, ledger sync · rebuild · stats, license status — speak --json. The agent is whatever you bring; galley never calls a model.

the cli

Every step of the round is a command.

galley edit <doc.md> Open a Markdown document in the browser as the rounds editor. Prints the URL. --on-revise '<cmd>' runs a command when Revise is pressed; --on-settle does the same when a live document goes quiet.
galley wait <doc.md> Block until the reviewer sends a round, then print the captured instructions with their quoted passages. --since re-arms from the last fingerprint; --timeout gives up. The agent-side loop for a session that is already in the room.
galley pending <doc.md> List the instructions the reviewer has started for the next round — through the running editor when there is one, from the file when there isn't.
galley ack <doc.md> --state <s> Return the round: received, working, answered, declined, or failed, with a --note for the reviewer and an optional --changes list naming which change answered which instruction.
galley cannot <doc.md> --why "…" Report the one instruction that could not be done. Recorded as a round of its own, document unchanged.
galley revise <doc.md> Send the round from the command line — wakes whoever is listening, a waiter or --on-revise. The same thing the button does.
galley channel The MCP channel server. Started with the agent session, it attaches to every editor the session opens under --scope and pushes each Revise, settle, and Approve into the session as an event. Exposes galley_ack and galley_channel_status as tools.
galley agent-prompt <doc.md> Print the protocol for an agent starting cold — the text to hand a session spawned by --on-revise. Static; galley never calls a model.
galley ledger sync · rebuild · stats The memory of the loop. Decisions are logged as they are made; sync brings the per-user index up to date, stats reads it.
galley serve <page.html> · comments The older surface: serve a standalone HTML page as a live document and collect comments beside it; comments prints them. Separate from the Markdown rounds editor.
galley version · license The build stamp; license activate <key> and license status.

licensing

Fourteen days, then one payment.

galley is Fair Core software (FCL-1.0-ALv2): each release converts to Apache-2.0 two years after it ships. The repository is private today — builds and keys come by mail.

14-day trial

Every build is fully functional for 14 days, stamped the first time you run a licensed command. No key, no sign-up, nothing withheld.

one-time license

$99, once. 12 months of updates. Every release from inside your window keeps working forever — no subscription, no renewal to keep what you have. Refunds are 14 days, no questions asked; the licence page has the terms.

verified offline

A key is a signed token your machine checks itself. The binary never talks to a server — not to verify, not to count, not to phone home.

The license covers the review loop — serve, comments, edit, pending, cannot, revise, wait, ack. The rest is free for good: agent-prompt, channel, ledger, license, version, help. Only the loop stops when the trial does.

Activation is one command: galley license activate <key>. galley license status says where you stand. A license needs galley 0.4.0 or newer — earlier builds run trial-only, so update before you activate. Keys are minted by hand while the repository is private — there is no checkout yet; mail court@subaud.io and one comes back.

setup

One static binary.

No runtime, no npm, no service. Releases — signed and notarized macOS builds, Linux builds, and the source under Fair Core — are cut and available on request while the repository is private. There is no public download page yet. The 14-day trial in every build is full-featured.
